Posted on 17th September
St John’s TV advert now airing on Sky
We’re excited to introduce our brand-new TV advert, now airing on Sky. The advert offers a glimpse into life at St John’s, with a snapshot of our vibrant school community, outstanding opportunities and commitment to helping every pupil find their...
Poetry comes alive with Kimba King! We were delighted to welcome acclaimed poet, author and spoken-word artist Kimba King to St John’s on Tuesday for an inspiring day of poetry workshops with pupils from Years 3 to 6.Through energetic performances and infectious enthusiasm, Kimba showed the boys that poetry is about so much more than finding words that rhyme. Through a series of engaging activities, they explored how rhythm, rhyme, imagery, wordplay and figurative language can bring their writing to life.The workshops encouraged pupils to experiment with language, develop their ideas and, most importantly, find their own voice as writers. It was wonderful to see them embracing the challenge, sharing their ideas and discovering just how much they can do with words.A huge thank you to Kimba for an inspiring and memorable day! #stjohnsprep #KimbaKing #spokenword #youngwriters
Making the most of the great outdoors!Our pupils love spending their break times in the woods, exploring, playing and making the most of the extensive outdoor space available to them.
Year 3 pupils are delving into the history of St John’s. This week, they discovered the story of the 1930 fire at Barrow Point House before putting their learning into practice by writing newspaper articles packed with some fantastic alliteration!#stjohnsprep #year3 #juniorhistorians #schoolhistory
We are excited to share our new TV advert currently airing on Sky! Have you seen it yet?
We warmly invite you to visit usOpen Morning | Friday 2 October 2026 from 9amhttps://www.st-johns.org.uk/admissions/visit-us/Welcoming girls and boys into Early Years from September 2027.
Our Year 5 mathematicians took their learning outside, exploring the school grounds and putting their knowledge of 3D shapes to the test. A great way to bring maths to life while making the most of our extensive outdoor space! #stjohnsprep #maths #LearningBeyondTheClassroom #outdoorlearning
We warmly invite you to visit usOpen Morning | Friday 2 October from 9amhttps://www.st-johns.org.uk/admissions/visit-us/Welcoming girls and boys into Early Years from September 2027.
On Friday, parents gathered in the Norman Hall for tea, cakes and a catch-up with friends, all in support of Macmillan Cancer Support.A huge thank you to the St John’s Association for organising such an enjoyable morning, and to everyone who donated so generously. We are delighted to have raised over £800 already!#stjohnsprep #stjohnsassociation #macmillancancersupport #coffeemorning
Our Nursery pupils have been talking about the people who are special to them and celebrating the wonderful things that make each of us unique.During Show & Tell, the children proudly shared pictures of the important people in their lives, while their fingerprint artwork captured the special people who make their families and homes unique.A lovely opportunity to celebrate love, belonging and the people who mean the most to us! #stjohnsprep #earlyyears #nurserylife #whatmakesusunique #family
The Art Department is in full swing! Year 3 boys have been learning all about backgrounds, middlegrounds and foregrounds, while some of our Year 4 artists have already completed their fantastic skeleton hand studies. Year 5 have been busy creating and exploring patterns, and our Year 6 boys are learning to paint like Monet, experimenting with his beautiful Impressionist style. It’s wonderful to see so much creativity, curiosity and talent on display.#stjohnsprep #artatschool #ArtDepartment #youngartists

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Mission and Aims | Independent School | St John's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St John’s, where every child is known, challenged, and inspired to forge their own path.
At St John’s, we provide the space to grow and the confidence to succeed. By integrating our exceptional natural environment with a bespoke academic journey, we nurture the individual character and ‘spark’ of every child empowering them to achieve excellence and make ambitious choices for their future.
Our Aims
Personalised Growth and Achievement
To know every child as an individual, providing a nurturing and bespoke educational journey that fosters self-confidence and enables every pupil to pursue academic excellence and personal aspirations.
Utilising our Unique Environment
To integrate our exceptional natural surroundings into the heart of the curriculum, using our extensive site to build resilience, support wellbeing, and ignite a lifelong sense of curiosity through outdoor exploration and play.
Academic Excellence and Aspiration
To maintain a rigorous focus on academic excellence, equipping pupils with a deep foundation of knowledge and a genuine joy for learning that prepares them for future scholarships and high-reaching success.
Informed Independence and Choice
To offer a broad and diverse range of opportunities that empower pupils and their families to make confident, informed decisions regarding senior school transitions, ensuring every child finds the right destination for their unique future.
Character and Values
To cultivate an environment where kindness, integrity, and good manners are paramount, developing well-rounded individuals with the “spark” and character required to thrive in the modern world.
The school motto, “vitam impendere vero” be true to yourself, stands behind St John’s values.
What this means for your child
We place kindness, confidence and character at the heart of the school, developing children who combine strong values and good manners with the confidence and spark to thrive.
Individualised Pathways
We know every child as an individual, nurturing and guiding them along a personalised pathway that supports their aspirations and enables them to grow in confidence, achieve academically and flourish.
An Outstanding Site
Our exceptional, and surprisingly extensive site and natural surroundings are an integral part of our school curriculum, giving children the space to explore, play and learn, and empowering their curiosity, resilience and wellbeing.
Academic Excellence
Through a strong focus on academic excellence, we give every child the knowledge, confidence and skills to embrace a lasting love and joy of learning and shape an aspirational future.
Choices
We provide breadth and choice throughout school life, preparing every child, and their family, with the confidence and independence to make informed, aspirational decisions about the right senior school destination for their unique future.
The Language of Learning
The Language of Learning is designed to help our pupils grow into well-rounded, happy, compassionate, and successful young people. Each of our core values is explored in depth, encouraging pupils to recognise, reflect upon, and apply these qualities both inside and outside the classroom. We believe that by embedding our values in daily school life, we not only support academic excellence but also nurture character, confidence, and a lifelong love of learning. Respect, honesty, fairness, and self-control are central to everything we do and a Language of Learning sits at the heart of teaching and learning across our school.
Pastoral Care

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Private School Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St John’s, an independent prep school on the Pinner/Northwood borders in Middlesex, for boys and girls aged 3–11. With a strong tradition of academic excellence, pastoral care and enrichment, we help every child to grow, achieve, and flourish, preparing them for the next stage of their journey and beyond. Our pupils regularly secure places at leading independent and selective senior schools, supported by a strong track record of academic progress and scholarship success.
This section of our website offers a closer look at what makes St John’s special, from our Headmaster’s Welcome and Aims and Ethos to our proud History, excellent Destination Schools and dedicated Staff Team.
Whether you are a prospective parent, a member of our community, or simply interested in our story, we invite you to explore and get to know St John’s, a place where children are inspired to learn and thrive.
More Information

pageCache.pageTitle: Heads Welcome | Private Day School Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
St John’s is a wonderful community where aspirational pupils enjoy learning and form joyful memories to last a lifetime. Set in a magnificent thirty-five acre estate overlooking London, our unique learning environment allows space for pupils to grow and realise their potential.
Our rich heritage as part of the Merchant Taylors’ family of schools was recently commemorated in our centenary celebrations. Traditional values of respect and kindness are blended with an innovative approach to teaching and learning; our ethos is both rounded as well as academically rigorous.
St John’s is a happy, vibrant and successful school where pupils’ individual talents are nurtured. Children who join the school work and play hard: Music, Drama and Sport are flourishing. Talents and passions are encouraged, indeed our senior groups are typically outstanding. Our contemporary curriculum and dedicated staff nurture and inspire the pupils.
St John’s seeks to work with families to develop rounded, resilient children. We seek to develop their character in the pursuit of academic excellence, laying the foundations for future success. Alumni progress smoothly to Merchant Taylors’ School, in addition to a variety of other leading independent schools. Here, their formative experiences at St John’s allow them to flourish as confident leaders.
I warmly invite you to visit us in order to see the wealth of opportunities your son or daughter can look forward to as they begin their journey towards becoming exceptional young people.
Mr T Jenkin, Headmaster

pageCache.pageTitle: Inspection Reports | Private School Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
At St John’s, we place great importance on the insights gained through regular independent inspections. These in-depth reviews provide parents with a clear, objective assessment of how effectively we are fulfilling our educational aims and responsibilities as a leading prep school.
Our most recent full inspections, involved a rigorous evaluation of the school’s operation alongside feedback from parents and pupils. The outcome was exceptionally positive across all areas, highlighting the strength of our teaching, pastoral care, leadership, and overall school environment.
Read the full ISI Inspection Reports to learn more about our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement in every aspect of school life.
St John’s 2026 Inspection Report
St John’s 2023 Inspection Report
Key Highlights (May 2023)
Overall Judgement: Excellent
St John’s was awarded the highest grade of ‘Excellent’ in all three core areas:
Pupil achievement was described as ‘exceptional’, with the inspectors highlighting that “pupils of all needs and abilities, including the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), are extremely successful in their learning.”
Teaching and Learning
Personal Development
Leadership and Governance
Early Years & Individual Support
The learning environment in our Nursery, Reception, and Pre-Prep was praised as “highly stimulating” with staff providing “highly effective planning” tailored to each child’s unique needs.
St John’s commitment to challenge and extend gifted pupils was highlighted, with inspectors noting that they are “very well prepared for scholarship examinations” and “the school’s successful record of entry into selective senior schools reflects the effectiveness of this preparation.”
Beyond the Classroom
Inspectors praised our broad and balanced curriculum and the exceptional achievements in extra-curricular activities, particularly in music, drama, and sport.
Pupils benefit from more than 50 clubs and after-school activities, as well as a wealth of outdoor learning opportunities.
Personal Development
The personal development of pupils was rated ‘excellent’, supported by a “friendly and caring atmosphere” and “high standards of behaviour.” The school was recognised for fostering strong spiritual, moral, social, and cultural values, with a clear emphasis on respect, tolerance, and equality.
“The school’s promotion of British values is embedded throughout, and pupils are taught to value and appreciate the beliefs and feelings of others.”
Safeguarding & Wellbeing
St John’s approach to safeguarding and welfare was described as “comprehensive and robust.” Inspectors highlighted our effective anti-bullying policy, which includes coverage of cyberbullying, and noted that pupils feel safe and supported.
Leadership & Governance
Leadership and governance were judged to be ‘excellent’. Inspectors praised:
“St John’s maintains strong relationships with parents, who are highly positive about the school’s provision.”

pageCache.pageTitle: History of St John's School | St John's School
pageCache.text:
St John’s has been a leading preparatory school for boys in Pinner, Harrow, and Northwood since 1920. Founded by Mr. Claude Norman, the school began in a single classroom at St John’s Church, Pinner. As it grew, it moved to The Briary in Moss Lane, then to Barrow Point House in 1927. A devastating fire in 1930 destroyed the building, but it was rebuilt and remained home to St John’s for the next 40 years.
Houses & The War (1935–1945)
The school’s House system was initially named after staff members. In 1935, they were renamed Lawrence, Lincoln, and Oates, with Churchill added after WWII.
During the war, Mr. Norman chose to keep the school in Pinner. Pupils recall watching air battles overhead and assisting in handling military supplies. Mr. Norman balanced his role as Headmaster with serving as Lieutenant Colonel in the Home Guard.
A New Home at Pinner Hill (1951–1970)
After Mr. Norman’s sudden passing in 1951, his son, Peter Norman, took over. With demand for places growing, he spent years searching for a larger site. In 1970, he successfully relocated the school to its current 30-acre home at Pinner Hill, securing Potter Street House (now The White House) against significant challenges. Over the following decades, sports fields, new buildings, and modern facilities were added.
Merchant Taylors & Expansion (1984–1999)
In 1984, St John’s became part of the Merchant Taylors’ Educational Trust, ensuring long-term stability. Under new governance, the school expanded significantly, with new teaching blocks, a Pre-Prep, a dedicated Music and Art wing, and improved sports facilities. By the 1990s, pupil numbers had reached 350.
Into the 21st Century (2000–2020)
The school continued to grow, introducing a state-of-the-art all-weather playing surface in 2006, expanding academic facilities, and enhancing outdoor spaces. In 2020, St John’s celebrated its Centenary with a Service of Thanksgiving and the opening of the Centenary Sports Hall and Treehouse.
Today & Beyond (2020–Present)
St John’s continues to evolve while staying true to its heritage. With a century of excellence behind us, we look forward to supporting our boys in their educational journey, shaping the future for generations of pupils to come.
Our Alumni

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Curriculum | Nursery Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
At St John’s Nursery, we provide a purposeful and stimulating start to school life for our youngest pupils. Our Nursery offers a structured and engaging curriculum within a warm, caring environment where children feel secure, supported, and ready to learn.
The Nursery curriculum follows the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, ensuring that each child experiences a broad and balanced programme across the seven key areas of learning:
Boys and girls benefit from a carefully planned combination of adult-led and child-initiated activities, with opportunities to learn individually, in small groups, and as a whole class. Teaching is responsive and personalised, allowing each boy to develop at his own pace, with clear progression throughout the year.
Early literacy and numeracy are gently introduced through stories, games, role-play and hands-on exploration, laying strong foundations for future academic success. The curriculum also includes specialist teaching in Physical Education and Music, enriching the children’s experiences and supporting their physical and creative development.
A strong emphasis is placed on personal, social and emotional growth, which underpins all aspects of learning in the early years. Through daily routines, modelling, and activities such as Circle Time, children are taught to listen, take turns, express themselves, and develop positive relationships. Values such as kindness, good manners and cooperation are reinforced throughout the day.
In the Nursery, our curriculum is not only about preparing boys and girls academically but also helping them become enthusiastic, curious, and resilient learners from the very start.

Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Curriculum
The Government document The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) provides the framework for the curriculum from birth to 5 years olds. It is based around four themes:
These themes are linked to important principles regarding children’s learning and development.
The curriculum consists of 7 areas of learning – 3 prime areas and 4 specific areas
A Unique child
Positive relationships
Enabling environments
Learning and development
Prime Areas
Communication and language Physical development Personal, social and emotional
Specific Areas
The seven areas are used to plan both the daily activities and the learning environment – indoors and out. Activities often provide opportunities for the boys to develop a number of skills across several areas of learning.
The seven areas are divided into early learning goals. It is expected that most children will have achieved these goals by the end of Reception although at St John’s many pupils will have exceeded them.
The teaching and experiences that your child will receive at St John’s will enable him to acquire, at their own pace, the skills, knowledge and attitudes necessary to achieve the Early Learning Goals within the seven areas of learning.

pageCache.text:
Learning at St John’s extends beyond the classroom door. Pupils are encouraged to explore their interests, take on new challenges, and discover their talents.
From music, drama and sport to team building and adventure activities, our co-curricular programme offers something for every pupil.
Educational trips
Each year, pupils at St John’s take part in carefully planned educational trips that enrich their learning, broaden their horizons, and bring the curriculum to life beyond the classroom.
Bi-annual ski trips
Night under canvas and teamwork challenge days
Responsibility and Leadership
As they progress up the school, pupils take on increasing levels of responsibility whether as School Council representatives, Eco Council members, or as positive role models for younger peers. These opportunities build confidence and help boys contribute meaningfully to school life.
In their final year, selected pupils may also be appointed a role within the Head Pupil Team, a prestigious group of roles that recognise leadership, maturity, and a strong commitment to the school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Outdoor Learning | St John's School
pageCache.text:
At St John’s, outdoor learning is at the heart of our Nursery experience. Every day, our youngest children have the opportunity to explore and engage with nature across a range of exceptional outdoor facilities. From imaginative play in our purpose-built tree house to hands-on discovery in the forest and outdoor classroom, children are encouraged to develop confidence, curiosity, and a sense of adventure.
Outdoor learning supports all areas of early development, strengthening gross and fine motor skills, enhancing communication and language, and providing rich opportunities for creative expression. Working together in outdoor spaces also helps children build cooperation and empathy, while open-ended play encourages risk-taking, resilience, and problem-solving.
Spending time in nature helps children feel calm, content, and emotionally secure; important foundations for learning both now and in the future.
Whether building dens, making mud pies, or simply enjoying the changing seasons, these regular immersive experiences help children develop a connection to the world around them and a lifelong love of learning.
Pastoral Care
More Information

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-Prep Outdoor Learning | Pre Prep School Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
At St John’s School, outdoor learning is an exciting part of early education. From the moment our Pre-Prep pupils step outside, they begin a journey of discovery, exploring nature, asking questions, and building confidence through hands-on experiences in the great outdoors.
Our outstanding outdoor spaces, including a dedicated forest area, an impressive tree house, educational bee hives, a tranquil well-being garden, and a brand-new outdoor classroom, spark imagination and bring learning to life.
Whether they’re hunting for mini-beasts, building dens, digging in the sand, or listening to stories around the fire, children develop creativity, teamwork, resilience, and a deep connection to the natural world.
Rain or shine, our pupils are always ready in their wellies and waterproofs, embracing every season with energy and joy.
At St John’s, we see the outdoors as a vibrant, living classroom where young minds grow, explore, and thrive.
Visit us to find out more, we will be delighted to welcome you.
Visit Us
More Information

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Outdoor Learning | Prep School | St John's School
pageCache.text:
Outdoor learning plays a vital role in the prep school experience, offering pupils opportunities to develop resilience, teamwork, and leadership skills beyond the traditional classroom setting.
Through a diverse programme of activities pupils are encouraged to explore, problem-solve, and deepen their understanding of the world around them.
Outdoor learning not only enhances academic learning but also encourages independence, personal growth, confidence, and a spirit of discovery that stays with our pupils for life.
From fieldwork and environmental studies to adventure-based challenges including survival skills and camping expeditions pupils are encouraged to think critically, work as a team, and connect with nature. Set across our extensive school ground, including a dedicated forest, outdoor classroom, enchanting tree house, the activities take full advantage of the natural environment and outstanding facilities St John’s has to offer.
Outdoor learning is one of the most eagerly anticipated aspects of school life. Pupils thrive on the excitement, challenge, and sense of achievement each adventure brings, enjoying the perfect complement to academic preparation for senior school.
More Information

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Prep School Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
At St John’s, we are committed to creating a safe, nurturing, and inclusive environment where every child feels respected, valued, and heard.
Our aim is to ensure that every child lives and learns in a setting where they feel secure and supported. All members of staff are dedicated to maintaining a culture of care, where children are encouraged to speak openly about any worries or concerns and know they will be listened to with care and understanding.
We place a strong emphasis on supporting children’s emotional wellbeing, helping them to develop resilience, confidence, and healthy relationships.
Through our Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education, we help children develop the knowledge and confidence to keep themselves safe, including online. Our curriculum also promotes understanding around safeguarding, e-safety, and inclusion.
More Information

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Care | Independent School Pinner | St John's School
pageCache.text:
St John’s Clubhouse wrap around care, is proudly run in-house under the school’s direct management. With familiar staff, clear routines and a focus on childrens’ wellbeing, we’re excited to offer a safe, happy start and finish to every school day.
Children are looked after in a dedicated space located on the ground floor of the Science Block on the school site. The facility includes a full kitchen and modern toilet facilities, and provides a safe, comfortable environment for before and after-school care.
Termly sessions can be booked in advance for Clubhouse Mornings and Clubhouse Tea. There is also the option for ad hoc bookings including on the day, subject to availability and appropriate staffing ratios.
Clubhouse Adventures offers a relaxed activity filled holiday camp during selected weeks of the school holidays. Children enjoy a range of activities, games and creative play with the experienced Clubhouse team.

St John’s Clubhouse Adventures extends the same warm, supportive environment during specific weeks of the school holidays. Children can look forward to creative projects, outdoor adventures and themed activity days, all delivered by our friendly staff. Clubhouse Adventures is welcomes all children. Food & Snacks
A range of nutritious food is provided daily.
Breakfast options include cereals, yoghurt, fresh fruit, toast and crumpets.
Afternoon snacks include crackers, sandwiches, pasta, whole meal wraps, beans on toast, fruit and vegetable platters.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is St John’s Clubhouse?
St John’s Clubhouse is a wraparound care provision under the direct management of St John’s School. All staff are familiar, trusted members of our school community, ensuring a safe and friendly environment. Children are cared for in our dedicated space with full kitchen and toilet facilities, situated on the ground floor of the Science block onsite at St John’s school.
What ages are accepted?
St John’s Clubhouse welcomes children from Nursery to Year 6 inclusive.
What are the opening hours?
Clubhouse Mornings (breakfast care): 7:30am – 8:30am
Clubhouse Tea (after school care): 3:00pm – 6:00pm
Clubhouse Adventures (holiday camp care): 9am – 4pm (selected dates during the school holidays)
How do I book a place?
St John’s parents can secure their space using the Bookings Tab in Involve.
New enquiries please email: office@st-johns.org.uk
Spaces are limited, so we recommend early registration.
What activities are on offer?
Activities vary by session and age and include creative arts, sports, board games, puzzles, role play, outdoor play, homework support and themed holiday adventures.
What food is provided?
Healthy breakfast options are provided during Clubhouse Mornings with options such as cereal, yogurt, fruit and toast.
Clubhouse Tea offers snacks including crackers, sandwiches, pasta, wraps suit and vegetable platters.
Children attending Clubhouse Adventure holiday camps bring in a nut free packed lunch.
Strict attention is paid to dietary requirements.
How is safety ensured?
All staff are DBS-checked, trained in safeguarding and first aid and experienced in working with children of all ages. Facilities meet all school safety standards. Children are carefully supervised and procedures are followed rigorously.
Can non-St John’s pupils join Clubhouse Adventures holiday camp?
Yes! St John’s Clubhouse Adventures holiday camp welcomes children who do not attend St John’s school.
What are the costs?
Prices start at £7 for Clubhouse Mornings (breakfast care) and £13 for Clubhouse Afternoons (after school care).
For individual quotes and for Clubhouse Adventures holiday camp dates, please email: office@st-johns.org.uk

Whether pupils are aiming for top-tier boarding schools, selective grammar schools, or highly regarded day schools, St John’s provides expert preparation and tailored support, making us one of the leading prep schools in Greater London for senior school destinations and scholarship success in academic, music, sport, art and design.
